questions.stem: A field team must carry a heavy instrument case up a long ramp and then bring it back down the same ramp. Explain what work gravity does on each leg of the trip.

answer.exemplar: Gravity pulls straight down, so while the team carries the case uphill it opposes the motion and does negative work, removing energy from the load. questions.stem: A field vehicle drives a rough track and the loose sample cases in the back slide about each time the driver brakes or accelerates. Explain what is happening and how a ratchet strap helps.

answer.exemplar: Each change in the vehicle's speed requires a net force on the cases, and that force comes from friction with the vehicle floor. Under braking the cases tend to keep their higher forward velocity and appear to slide forward, and under acceleration they tend to keep their lower velocity and slide backward. A ratchet strap works by adding a tension that only resists the relative sliding, so it supplies the missing net force and keeps the cases from moving relative to the vehicle.

questions.explanation: The cases resist the changes in motion caused by braking and acceleration, so they slide unless friction can accelerate them. A strap adds tension opposing the sliding, supplying the needed net force.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_I
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a tripod loses grip as a slope steepens
questions.stem: A field team sets up a camera tripod on a slope and finds that the legs slip when the slope steepens. Explain what limits the grip and how steepening the slope changes it.

answer.exemplar: The maximum static friction at each leg is the coefficient of static friction multiplied by the normal force at that leg, and on a slope the normal force is only the component of the load perpendicular to the ground, which shrinks as the slope steepens. At the same time the component of the weight pulling the tripod downhill grows, because it scales with the sine of the angle. One term weakens while the other strengthens, so a slope that was safe can become unsafe purely by changing its angle.

questions.explanation: The grip limit falls with the normal force as the slope steepens, while the downhill pull grows with the sine of the angle. A stable tripod can become unstable as the slope grows.
questions.hint: Compare the downhill pull with the shrinking grip.
